cards.explanation: The answer is home. Luke says a woman named Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). She's the one who does the welcoming, friends.

The answer is that Mary sits at His feet listening to Him. Luke says she "…sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) She sits down close to Jesus and listens. Sitting still and listening is what the text shows her doing.

The answer is that her sister left her to serve alone. Martha says, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) She's got a lot to do and one set of hands. I think she feels stretched thin, and honestly, who hasn't been there?
The answer is True. Martha says, "Tell her to help me!" (Luke 10:40) She says it right to Jesus. She asks Him to be the one to tell Mary, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things." (Luke 10:41) Hear how He says her name twice. I think that's a gentle way to start. He sees what's on her plate and He says it out loud.

The answer is only one. Jesus says, "But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:42) Martha has many things going on, and Jesus puts one thing next to all of them. That's a short list to remember, bakers.

The answer is that it will not be taken away from her. Jesus says Mary "…has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) That's a promise about what she has. Nobody can swipe it, not even a long to-do list.

The answer is False. Martha asks Jesus to tell Mary to help (Luke 10:40), but Jesus doesn't send her anywhere. He says Mary "…has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) The text shows no sending at all, friends.
